title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'An ensemble of DNs controls landing via a core premotor circuit' / Fig. 1E-G, Fig. 2A-B,F
quote: In summary, DNp07, DNp10, DNp47, and DNg79 drive extensions of all six legs as part of the landing response
mapping_basis: Paper names DNp07, a MANC/Namiki type name; driver line SS02276 maps to DNp07 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm LED, 50 ms pulses, 150 microW/mm2, 10 s interstimulus interval
coordination_notes: Simultaneous extension of all six legs with front legs reaching beyond the head (landing response); single extension, not cyclic
notes: Activation during tethered flight; leg tarsal tips tracked with DeepLabCut. Single extension movement, so no leg rhythm. Paper also reports a connectome-constrained leaky integrate-and-fire simulation of landing DN recruitment (Fig. S4-1B), hence saw_simulation_score=true; that simulation was not used as evidence. DNp07 activation also reduced wingbeat frequency and stopped flight in 6/19 flies.

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila

quote: Percent of flies that perform landing responses (based on front leg extensions greater than dashed line from Fig. 1E) using two different driver lines for DNp07.

other_cell_types: unspecified background expression (Namiki 2018 quality B, ~2 off-target cell types)
coordination_notes: Landing-type front leg extension beyond head, as for the first DNp07 line (Fig. S2-1A-C, H)
penetrance: 100% of flies performed landing responses (Fig. S1-1C)
notes: figure: Fig. S1-1C bar plot shows landing probability near 100% for both DNp07_1 and DNp07_2; second driver line for the same type, coded as a separate experiment. Simulation (leaky integrate-and-fire model, Fig. S4-1B) seen in this paper but not used as evidence.

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DNs within an ensemble promote behavioral variants' / Fig. 1F, Fig. 2A-B,F-G
quote: DNp10 and DNp47 consistently drove more laterally-directed middle and hind leg movements compared to all other DNs
mapping_basis: Paper names DNp10, a MANC/Namiki type name; driver line SS01608 maps to DNp10 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm LED, 50 ms pulses, 150 microW/mm2, 10 s interstimulus interval
coordination_notes: Landing-type extension of all six legs but with less anterior rotation of middle and hind legs than DNp07
notes: Single leg extension (landing response), not cyclic stepping, so all leg rhythms 'no'. In non-flying walking flies DNp10 activation caused wing raising/flicking (Fig. S2-2G), with no leg movement described. Simulation present in paper (Fig. S4-1B) but not used as evidence.

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DNs within an ensemble promote behavioral variants' / Fig. 1F, Fig. 2F-G
quote: DNp10 and DNp47 consistently drove more laterally-directed middle and hind leg movements compared to all other DNs
mapping_basis: Paper names DNp47, a MANC/Namiki type name listed in type_list.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm LED, 50 ms pulses, 150 microW/mm2, 10 s interstimulus interval
coordination_notes: Landing-type extension of all six legs; less anteriorly directed middle leg extension than DNp07/DNg79

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DNs within an ensemble promote behavioral variants' / Fig. 2F, Fig. S2-1I
quote: During DNg79 activation, the front leg coxae rotated forwards and underneath the head, followed by a dorsally directed, lateral extension of the distal segments
mapping_basis: Paper names DNg79, a MANC type in type_list.csv; line SS81942 maps to DNg79 (with DNg31) in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm LED, 50 ms pulses, 150 microW/mm2, 10 s interstimulus interval
coordination_notes: Greater front and middle leg extension than any other landing DN; front legs lifted above the head
notes: line_specificity multi_dn because driver_lines.csv lists SS81942 as labelling 'DNg31, DNg79'; the paper itself calls it a DNg79 line. Single extension sequence, not rhythmic stepping. Activation also deflected the abdomen downward. Simulation present in paper but not used as evidence.

title: Parallel neuronal ensembles control behavior across sensorimotor levels in Drosophila

title: Control of walking direction by descending and dopaminergic neurons in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'A neuronal substrate for forward and curve walking' / Fig. 2B-H
quote: Activation drove consistent increases in forward walking speed, leading to longer walking trajectories during the period of red light exposure compared to ‘empty’ controls
mapping_basis: Paper says SS02553 'labels DNp17 (among other neurons)'; driver_lines.csv lists SS02553 as AMBIGUOUS (DNp17;DNut046) with DNp17 as the written type, so confidence is medium.
stimulation: 625 nm red LED, 10 s pulses at 0.41-4.07 mW/cm2 (strongest 4.07 mW/cm2), 60 s interstimulus interval
sensory_condition: freely walking in UFO arena under 0.11 mW/cm2 white light
coordination_notes: Meandering/curve walking with increased tortuosity index; legs not individually tracked
n_flies_note: N = 17 SS02553>CsChrimson flies vs N = 18 empty controls, 9 trials per intensity
notes: Walking speed from centroid tracking (TRex), no leg tracking, so leg rhythms inferred from walking (PROTOCOL s.3) and confidence capped at medium. The paper attributes this phenotype to DopaMeander rather than DNp17 (see record 0008); record is kept because the line labels DNp17 and is a non-specific line. The paper's linear-nonlinear models of neural activity are its own models, not a connectome activation screen; no rhythm score, rank or driver call was seen.

title: Control of walking direction by descending and dopaminergic neurons in Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'DopaMeander drives the walking phenotype of SS02553' / Fig. 3D-E
quote: Flies expressing CsChrimson in DNp17 displayed a broad range of forward velocities between 1 and 12 mm/s with a median of 5 mm/s.
mapping_basis: SPARC subsets of the SS02553 line, with DNp17 identified by post-hoc tdTomato staining; driver_lines.csv lists SS02553 as AMBIGUOUS (DNp17;DNut046).
stimulation: 625 nm red light, 10 s pulses at 4.07 mW/cm2
type_coverage: stochastic SPARC2 subsets (~15% or ~50% of labelled cells)
other_cell_types: other SS02553 neuron types 3-8 in some flies
coordination_notes: Flies with DNp17 but not DopaMeander labelled walked significantly slower than those with DopaMeander (Fig. 3E)
penetrance: variable; DNp17-only flies showed much weaker speed increases than DopaMeander flies
n_flies_note: 26 flies dissected and analysed overall; 17 expressed CsChrimson in some neurons, 9 in none
notes: Stochastic (SPARC) activation of subsets of the SS02553 line; the authors conclude DNp17 'increases walking speed only slightly, if at all' and that DopaMeander drives the phenotype. Centroid tracking only, no leg tracking, hence medium confidence.

title: Remote control of behavior through genetically targeted photostimulation of neurons.
quote: Photostimulation of neurons in the giant fiber system elicited the characteristic escape behaviors of jumping, wing beating, and flight
mapping_basis: 'Giant fiber system' maps to the Giant Fiber (DNp01) per synonyms.csv (DNp01 = GF/Giant Fiber), but the abstract names a 'system' rather than a single cell type, so medium.
stimulation: laser light (broad illumination); details not available in the abstract
notes: Abstract only; publisher full text (cell.com, sciencedirect) returned HTTP 403 and the article is not in PMC/Europe PMC, so no figure or results detail was reachable. Jumping is a single movement, so all leg rhythms coded 'no' per PROTOCOL section 3; the abstract gives no leg description beyond jumping.
